topic: Components of Environment: Biotic and Abiotic

objectives.statement: Classify components into biotic and abiotic

misconceptions.statement: Clouds move so they are living
misconceptions.correction: Movement is not life; clouds are abiotic

misconceptions.statement: Soil is not part of the environment
misconceptions.correction: Soil is an abiotic component that supports life

engagement_hook.prompt: What living and non-living things did you see on your way to school today?

teacher_activities: Ask students what they saw on the way to school and list responses
student_activities: Share one living and one non-living observation aloud

teacher_activities: Give each group a set of picture cards to sort into biotic and abiotic
student_activities: Sort the cards in groups and justify each placement to the group

teacher_activities: Introduce producers, consumers and decomposers using the sorted cards
student_activities: Copy the concept map and add one local example to each category

teacher_activities: Pose the formative questions and check answers with the class
student_activities: Answer the quiz individually then peer-check

advanced: Build a food chain from the cards

formative_checks.prompt: Which of these is a biotic component?
Name one producer found near your school.

instructions: Draw four things near your home and label each B or A
Mark which are producers, consumers, decomposers

objectives.statement: Explain that sound is produced by vibration
Investigate how sound travels through a medium

misconceptions.statement: Sound can travel through empty space with no medium
misconceptions.correction: Sound needs a medium such as air, water or a solid to travel
Loudness is amplitude; speed depends on the medium, not volume

engagement_hook.prompt: Place your hand on your throat and hum — what do you feel while the sound lasts?

teacher_activities: Ring a temple bell and ask what makes the sound and when it stops
student_activities: Touch the bell to feel the vibration and describe it

teacher_activities: Guide groups to make a rubber-band guitar and a paper-cup string phone
student_activities: Pluck the band and speak through the string phone, noting what carries sound

teacher_activities: Link vibration to sound and introduce the idea of a medium
student_activities: Draw how vibration reaches the ear through air

teacher_activities: Ask the formative questions and discuss the string-phone evidence
student_activities: Answer the quiz and explain one observation from the activity

struggling: Give a ready-made string phone to test
on_level: Build and test the string phone
advanced: Test whether the string phone works when the string is slack and explain why

formative_checks.prompt: Sound can travel through a vacuum.
Through which does sound travel fastest?

instructions: List three vibrating objects at home that make sound
Write one sentence on what each vibration moves through
